title: What did not pass
question: Which money files were voted down, tabled or vetoed, and did the same organization or property come back?
finding: Very little fails. Of 3,483 money files with a final vote the Board voted down 3: Appropriation - Cost of Doing Business for Non-Profit Agencies - General City Responsibility - … (5 to 6, 2015); Sale of City Property - 30 Van Ness Holdings, LLC - 30 Van Ness … (4 to 7, 2015); Amended and Restated Office Lease - Retroactive - The Lighthouse Building LLC - 1155 … (0 to 11, 2023). The Mayor vetoed 3 appropriations the Board had passed by 6 to 5, 7 to 4, 7 to 4, and the record shows no later roll call on any of them. In committee a motion to recommend failed 3 times, and 19 files were tabled, 16 of them in committee. For 2 of these files a later money file names the same organization or street address. The vote tables print the result “Fail” on 16 roll calls on money files in all: 7 are motions to amend, continue or pass part of a file, and 3 look like slips in the record.
how: Every roll call on a money file with the printed result Fail, every roll call to table one, and every file whose status in the legislative record is Vetoed. “What followed” looks for money files introduced after that vote that name the same organization (public bodies left out) or the same street address in their title, and gives the first two with what the Board did. For a motion to amend or continue that failed, it gives the file’s own final vote instead.
limits: Few failures at the vote does not mean few refusals: a file can also be withdrawn, amended, or left in committee until the Clerk files it as inactive under Rule 3.42, and none of that produces a roll call. 109 money files have the status Filed and 22 Killed. Tabling is a motion the rules describe as made “for the purpose of postponing temporarily or postponing indefinitely a matter before the Board or a committee”. A later file naming the same organization or address is not necessarily the same proposal: the match is on the name or the address only. A veto is the Mayor’s power; whether an override was attempted is not in these tables. Parties that are private persons are not named. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
